title: Raphaël Tinarrage — Topological Data Analysis with Persistent Homology
note: Primary teaching sequence, Lessons 0–11. Free lecture materials, videos and practical notebooks are linked from the course page.

title: ETH Zürich — Introduction to Topological Data Analysis, 2026
note: Formal reference. Mathematical foundations, homology, persistence, point-cloud complexes, distances/stability, Mapper and advanced extensions. The page lists discrete mathematics, algorithms/data structures and linear algebra prerequisites.

title: Sidney A. Morris — Topology Without Tears
note: Free author-hosted topology book and accompanying proof/topology videos. Use for open sets, continuity, connectedness and compactness.

title: Richard Hammack — Book of Proof
note: Free author-hosted proof textbook. Use sets, logic, quantifiers, proof methods, relations and functions.

title: MIT OpenCourseWare — Gilbert Strang, Linear Algebra
note: Free lectures, assignments and solutions. Focus on vector spaces, nullspaces, column spaces, rank, bases and linear maps.

title: Thomas W. Judson — Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications
note: Author-hosted open textbook. Select basic groups, homomorphisms, group actions, vector spaces and fields; a full second algebra course is not a prerequisite here.

title: Allen Hatcher — Algebraic Topology
note: Author-hosted free electronic book subject to its stated terms. Use geometric preliminaries, fundamental-group introduction and homology. Linked only; not redistributed.

title: Frédéric Chazal and Bertrand Michel — An introduction to Topological Data Analysis
note: Primary author paper connecting metric spaces, complexes, persistence, Mapper, stability and statistical interpretation. Read critically after the small exact examples.

title: scikit-learn — Common pitfalls and recommended practices
note: Primary library guidance on fitting transformations on training data and preventing evaluation leakage.

title: Ioannis Diamantis — The Shape of Data: Topology Meets Analytics
note: Free author paper for the final critique. The paper’s proposed stability index is not a replacement for algebraic stability or a statistical-significance argument.

title: UCI — Iris
note: Dataset provenance and CC BY 4.0 license metadata. The included array is scikit-learn’s documented corrected variant.

title: UCI — Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits
note: Dataset provenance and CC BY 4.0 metadata. Full UCI collection and original writer-separated split are distinct from this course’s subset and new image split.

title: scikit-learn — Bundled small datasets and their variants
note: Confirms bundled real Iris and digits descriptions, 1,797 digit images, 8×8 values, original-test-set provenance, and the Iris corrections.

title: Ripser.py — ripser API reference
note: Primary reference for points/distance matrices, maxdim, coefficient field, cutoff and returned diagrams. Optional package not installed in the build environment.

title: GUDHI — Rips and Delaunay/alpha manuals
note: Primary complex-construction reference. Alpha details: https://gudhi.inria.fr/python/latest/delaunay_complex_user.html . Default alpha values use squared-radius units. Optional library not executed in this build.

title: GUDHI — Cubical complex manual
note: Primary reference for square/cubical input semantics. Our core uses its own explicit filtration-preserving triangle subdivision, not an unexecuted GUDHI call.

title: Python — An Informal Introduction to Python
note: Official introductory syntax reference: arithmetic, strings, indexing and lists. Live documentation may target a newer version than the tested Python 3.13.5 runtime.
